Cluster 2 · Double-Pruning Physiology

April & October Grape Pruning: Bud Fruitfulness, Sub-Canes & Dormex

Direct Answer · April & October Grape Pruning

Tropical Indian vineyards follow double pruning and single cropping: April (Foundation) Pruning to 0–2 basal buds drives fruit-bud differentiation at 35–60 DAP, while October (Forward) Pruning to 5–10 buds plus Dormex 50% SL (30–40 ml/L) within 24–48 hrs harvests in 120–160 days [ICAR-NRCG; MPKV].

Interactive Pruning-to-Harvest Stage Stepper

Tap any pruning or fruiting stage to check exact DAP window, daily drip water (L/vine/day), fertigation focus, canopy task, and EU MRL/disease alerts [ICAR-NRCG].

April Foundation Pruning & Shoot Flush

Apr 0–30 DAP
Daily Drip Water
6–10 L / vine / day
Nutrient Focus
Basal 40–50 t/ha FYM + 30% annual P (SSP); 25% N + 10% P + 10% K via Urea + 19:19:19 / MAP
Canopy & PGR Task
Back-prune to 0–2 basal buds, strip loose trunk bark, thin shoots at 15–30 DAP to 30–40 uniform shoots/vine.
Top Stage Alert: Flea Beetle (Udadya) & Anthracnose Alert Inspect swollen buds for Flea Beetle (>5/vine ETL). Strip bark pre-pruning and protect young shoots against Anthracnose with Copper (2–2.5 g/L) [ICAR-NRCG].

Fruit-Bud Differentiation Window (Critical)

Apr 31–60 DAP
Daily Drip Water
8–12 L / vine / day (NO drought stress!)
Nutrient Focus
HARD N-BRAKE (5% N only!) + 15% P + 10% K via MKP (0:52:34) + SOP (0:0:50). Collect 45 DAP petiole sample.
Canopy & PGR Task
Pinch sub-canes mechanically at 5–7 leaves + 6-BA (10 ppm) / Uracil (50 ppm). Keep Y-trellis open for summer sunlight on basal buds.
Top Stage Alert: Excess N or CCC MRL Trap Excess Nitrogen or canopy shade during Days 31–60 turns fruit buds into blind tendrils. Avoid repeated Chlormequat Chloride (CCC/Lihocin) sprays — top EU MRL failure trigger [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA].
Open full guide for this stage →

Monsoon Cane Ripening & Wood Hardening

Apr 61–120 DAP
Daily Drip Water
Rainfed / 4–8 L / vine / day in dry spells
Nutrient Focus
5% N + 0% P + 10% K via SOP (0:0:50) + MgSO4 / Boron check to ripen 8–10 mm brown canes.
Canopy & PGR Task
Maintain 30°–40° Extended Y-Trellis airflow; remove excess water shoots and diseased monsoon foliage.
Top Stage Alert: Monsoon Downy Mildew & Arm Dieback Protect cane leaves from Downy Mildew (Kevda) with Bordeaux (0.5–1%) / Copper so carbohydrates store properly. Paste trunk pruning wounds with Copper oxychloride against Botryosphaeria dieback [ICAR-NRCG].
Open full guide for this stage →

October Forward Pruning, Dormex & Bloom

Oct 1–40 DAP
Daily Drip Water
6–10 L / vine / day
Nutrient Focus
25% N + 35% P + 15% K via MAP (12:61:00) + Urea. Pre-bloom 0.1% B + 0.25% Zn prevents shot berries.
Canopy & PGR Task
Test bud fruitfulness under microscope; prune 5–10 buds; apply Dormex 50% SL (30–40 ml/L) WITHIN 24–48 hrs. Apply GA3 10 ppm pre-bloom (pH 5.5–6.0).
Top Stage Alert: 48-Hr Dormex Deadline & Wet-Panicle Downy Mildew Waiting past 48 hrs after pruning ruins uniform sprouting. Unseasonal Oct rain causes tendril reversion ("fillage") and explosive Downy Mildew — rotate FRAC groups immediately [ICAR-NRCG].
Open full guide for this stage →

Capfall Thinning, Fruit Set & 6 mm Stage

Oct 41–70 DAP
Daily Drip Water
10–14 L / vine / day
Nutrient Focus
25% N + 10% P + 20% K + Calcium Nitrate (TANK B ONLY!) + KNO3 (13:0:45) + SOP. Collect Oct full-bloom petioles.
Canopy & PGR Task
Capfall GA3 15–20 ppm (50% & 90% capfall); balance load to 35–40 bunches/vine; scissor-thin berries to 80–100/bunch.
Top Stage Alert: Thrips Scab & Tank A/B Lock Thrips (>5/shoot) scar 3–6 mm berries with corky russet rings — hang blue sticky traps (25/ha) and rotate Spinosad/Emamectin per Annexure-5 PHI. Never mix Ca(NO3)2 with SO4/PO4.
Open full guide for this stage →

Berry Sizing & EU-Safe GA3/CPPU Dip

Oct 71–105 DAP
Daily Drip Water
14–22 L / vine / day (Peak demand)
Nutrient Focus
15% N + 0% P + 25% K via KNO3 + SOP + MgSO4. STOP ALL NITROGEN BY 95–105 DAP!
Canopy & PGR Task
Berry dip at 3–4 mm & 6–7 mm: GA3 30–40 ppm OR GA3 25–30 ppm + CPPU 1–2 ppm strictly ONCE. Skirt bunches / apply bags.
Top Stage Alert: Never Exceed 2 ppm CPPU & Stop Mancozeb/Phosphonates Early CPPU >2 ppm causes thick crunchy skin, <16°Brix, berry shatter & EU MRL violation. Release Cryptolaemus (1,500–2,500/ha) for mealybugs; halt Fosetyl-Al & Mancozeb per NRCG Annexure-5 PHI.
Open full guide for this stage →

Veraison, Sugar Build & GrapeNet Harvest

Oct 106–150 DAP
Daily Drip Water
8–12 L / vine / day (Taper 7–10 d pre-harvest)
Nutrient Focus
0% N + 0% P + 10–15% K via SOP (0:0:50) ONLY to build >=16°Brix & firm pedicels.
Canopy & PGR Task
Check NRL-NRCG residue clearance 15–20 d pre-pick. Harvest >=16°Brix (~20:1 sugar/acid, 16–18 mm) for EU export or 22–24°Brix for Sangli raisins.
Top Stage Alert: Pink Berry, Cracking & Cold-Chain Rule Irregular veraison drip triggers berry cracking. Shade exposed clusters against Pink Berry. Pre-cool export cartons (4.5–5 kg + SO2 pad) within 4–6 hrs to 0–1°C (90–95% RH) [APEDA 2026].

April (Foundation / Kharad) Pruning & Days 31–60 Bud Differentiation

Direct Answer · April Pruning & Fruit-Bud Differentiation

Prune back to 0–2 basal buds in March–April, strip loose bark, and thin to 30–40 shoots/vine by 15–30 DAP. Between Days 31–60, cut Nitrogen hard, prevent drought stress, pinch sub-canes mechanically at 5–7 leaves, and keep sunlight hitting basal buds so fruitful clusters form for October [ICAR-NRCG; MPKV].

Sub-Cane Pinching Beats Repeated CCC Sprays

Mechanical pinching at 5–7 leaves paired with 6-BA (10 ppm) or Uracil (50 ppm) at 45 DAP builds compact fruitful sub-canes cleanly without triggering EU Chlormequat Chloride (CCC / Lihocin) residue violations.

April Days 35–60 Drought & Shade Warning

Two mistakes ruin October yield 5 months in advance: (1) moisture stress during April Days 35–60, and (2) lush shaded Bower canopies fed excess Urea. Both convert flower primordia into blind tendrils.

October (Forward / God) Pruning, 48-Hr Dormex Rule & Weather Shielding

Direct Answer · October Pruning & Dormex Timing

Run a microscope bud-fruitfulness test before pruning 5–10 buds in late September–October, then swab/spray Hydrogen Cyanamide (Dormex 50% SL at 30–40 ml/L = 1.5–2.0% a.i.) within 24–48 hours. Avoid early September rain ("fillage" & Downy Mildew) and late November cold (<10°C shot berries) [ICAR-NRCG; MH Protocols 2026].

UV Plastic Cover & Crop-Load Discipline

Installing UV plastic covers (580 kLy, 25% thermicity) shields Oct–Feb clusters from unseasonal rain, Downy Mildew, and <10°C cold snaps while keeping canopy microclimate manageable. Always cap crop load at 35–40 bunches/vine — over-cropping stalls sugar below 16°Brix and exhausts next year’s canes [ICAR-NRCG; MANAGE]. *(Note: Tamil Nadu / Bengaluru vineyards run double pruning + double cropping for 2 harvests/year.)*

April & October Pruning FAQs

Why do April Days 31–60 decide October bunch yield?

Microscopic fruit-bud differentiation inside the 0–2 basal cane buds happens 35–60 days after April pruning. Canopy shade, moisture stress, or excess Nitrogen during Days 31–60 turns fruit buds into blind fruitless tendrils [ICAR-NRCG; MPKV].

Within how many hours of October pruning must Dormex (Hydrogen Cyanamide) be applied?

Apply Dormex 50% SL at 30–40 ml/L (1.5–2.0% active) strictly within 24–48 hours of October forward pruning. Delaying past 48 hours sharply reduces uniform bud break; exceeding 40 ml/L risks bud burn [ICAR-NRCG].

What happens if October pruning is done too early in September or too late in November?

Pruning too early in September exposes tender flower panicles to monsoon rain, causing tendril reversion ("fillage") and explosive Downy Mildew. Pruning in late November risks cold-snap dormancy (<10°C) and high shot-berry incidence [ICAR-NRCG; MH Protocols 2026].

How many bunches per vine should be retained for >=16°Brix export grapes?

Balance crop load to 35–40 uniform bunches per vine (80–100 scissor-thinned berries per bunch). Over-cropping delays veraison, drops sugar below 16°Brix, shrinks berry diameter, and weakens next season’s canes [ICAR-NRCG].
